record_scope_reconstruction: Two Táchira pedestrian bridges, Simón Bolívar and Francisco de Paula Santander, not all Colombia–Venezuela border. Humanitarian exceptions fromMarch remain.

source_checks.finding: Reuters23Feb reports temporaryTáchira shutdown lateFriday and distinguishes pre-existing vehicle bans from aid confrontation.
AP8Jun actual thousandscrossing two bridges, explicitly naming Simón Bolívar and Francisco de Paula Santander. APcopies not independent.

sites.name: Simón Bolívar international road bridge
sites.coordinate_method: OSM bridge reference coordinates reproduced by Mapcarta
sites.precision: approximate bridge area, about 100 m; not customs gate footprint
sites.evidence_note: Inspected geographical page names OSM way 871456442 as the road bridge over the Táchira linking San Antonio and La Parada; excludes same-name Barranquilla bridge. Original event accounts name the same international bridge.

sites.name: Francisco de Paula Santander international bridge
sites.coordinate_method: DMS conversion from inspected Wikidata coordinate
sites.precision: approximate bridge; 210m span; secondary coordinate evidence
sites.evidence_note: Inspected Q6091179 revision2134981114: 7°54′59″N 72°27′46.001″W; named road bridge across Táchira linking Cúcuta and Ureña. Different from same-name Magdalena bridge. Wikidata coordinate statement has no cited reference: qualified geographic reference, not a surveyed checkpoint.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Ordinary pedestrian phase at both bridges; prior vehicle bans and informalpaths excluded.
phase_decisions.date_scope_check: 22–23Feb onset uncertainty and8Jun observed pedestrian reopening retained; later humanitarian passages do not erase ordinary restriction.
